To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Ser residue influences the assembly and stability of a transmembrane helical protein dimer by forming hydrogen bonds with backbone carbonyl oxygens.
a Ser residue located adjacent to a Pro residue can influence the structure and stability in a Pro-kink of transmembrane helices by hydrogen bonding with the backbone carbonyl of the helix.

the conserved Ser in cytochrome b559' is crucial for assembly and stabilization and that the hydrogen bond between the polar hydroxyl of Ser and a backbone carbonly oxygen in the transmembrane helical dimer is important for defining the actual bending angle
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and assembly of integral membrane proteins.
the role of Pro and Ser residues in defining the structure and function of transmembrane α helices and their oligomeric assemblies.
the role of a conserved Ser residue in stabilizing transmembrane helical structures and with its influence on protein stability and folding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrogen bond between the Ser and the backbone carbonyl is crucial to stabilize the Pro-kinked helix.
the Ser residue is crucial to the stability of the cytochrome b (559)' dimer.
the hydrogen bond between a Ser and the backbone carbonyl of an adjacent Pro-kinked helix is important to maintain the correct conformation of the helices in a dimeric transmembranous protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ser residues can influence the structure and stability by forming intrahelical hydrogen bonds with a backbone carbonyly oxygen and that the impact of this hydrogen bond is most pronounced when it is localized adjacent to a transmembrane Pro-kink.
the Ser residue is important for the assembly and stability of the dimer, and for its function in the membrane, as a result of a subtle change in the structure of a transmembrane helical domain.
Ser is an important residue to stabilize the Pro-kink in transmembrane proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a highly conserved serine residue in the transmembrane domain of a cytochrome is important for the assembly and stability of the protein.
a Ser hydrogen bond may stabilize transmembrane helices and that this stabilization may be important for the folding of a transmembrane protein and for the stability of its holo form.
Ser residues in transmembrane helices are more likely to be involved in stabilizing the protein structure than in modulating its function.
